name: Victorian
summary: The middle-class room of the industrial century. Machine-made pattern covers walls, floors and furniture; dark, saturated colours, heavy curtains and many objects make a dense, enclosed parlour around the hearth.

philosophy.core_thesis: A home shows the taste, the travels and the respectability of its family; more objects and more pattern mean more comfort.
design_principles: Divide the wall into dado, filling and frieze, each with its own paper or paint.
Use deep, saturated colours: crimson, bottle green, plum and brown, with gold.
Layer textiles: a fitted carpet, a rug on it, a tablecloth on the table and a fringed cover on the mantel.
Group chairs in several conversation circles, not one; the room holds many zones.
Display collections on the mantel, on whatnots and in cabinets.
Hang pictures close together on a picture rail, frame to frame.
Filter the daylight through three layers at the window: blind, lace and heavy drapes.
anti_patterns: White or pale walls in the main rooms
A single centred group of furniture with empty floor around it

composition.plan_logic: A closed room with the hearth on a side wall. Several furniture groups fill the floor; a centre table stands under a gasolier.
composition.focal_point: The hearth with an overmantel mirror and a crowded mantelpiece on the left wall.

rules.rule: Make the hearth the focal point and frame it with an overmantel and a dense mantel display.
Layer the window in 3 textiles and the floor in 2; set furniture in front of furniture.
Mix many patterns, but keep them in one family of deep colours.
Divide the wall into dado, filling and frieze, each with a different paper.
Group chairs in several small circles and objects in dense clusters.
Mirror the overmantel, the vases and the chairs about the hearth only.
Give the walls a deep pattern, the woodwork and furniture brown, and gold and crimson the accents.
Light pools from a gasolier over the centre table and from shaded lamps; leave the corners dim.
Use large, heavy furniture with deep upholstery; chairs are broad and button-backed.
Leave narrow routes between the groups.
Shoot the room level, with a three-quarter view from the door toward the hearth.

zoning.circulation: Narrow, curved routes between dense furniture groups.

palette.distribution: Deep patterned wallpaper on the filling, dark wood on the dado and furniture, and crimson, gold and green in textiles and frames.

lighting.strategy: A low, warm interior. A central gasolier and many shaded lamps give separate pools of light; the walls and corners stay dark.
lighting.daylight: Daylight passes a roller blind, lace and heavy drapes; the room is dim by day.

layers.source: oil-style table lamp with a fringed shade
bay window behind lace and drapes

materials.finish: Polished dark wood, glossy tiles in the hearth, deep-pile textiles.
materials.texture_contrast: Soft, deep-pile textiles against polished wood and glazed tile, at about 1:1.

furniture.silhouette: Heavy, curved and carved pieces with deep button upholstery, turned legs and fringes.
furniture.arrangement: Several groups across the floor; small tables, footstools and whatnots fill the gaps.
key_pieces: round centre table with a cloth

textiles.pattern: Dense florals, damask and Turkey carpets; pattern on pattern in one colour family.
textiles.windows: Three layers: a roller blind, lace curtains and heavy velvet drapes with a pelmet and tie-backs.

objects.approach: Many objects show the family's taste and travels: collections, souvenirs, plants and portraits.
objects.grouping: Dense clusters on the mantel, on shelves and on tables; pictures frame to frame.
items: mantel clock under a glass dome

implementation.brief: A dim parlour with bottle-green damask paper above a dark wood dado. A marble hearth with an overmantel mirror and a crowded mantel stands on the left wall; a button-back sofa, balloon-back chairs and a round clothed table sit on a Turkey carpet under a brass gasolier.
implementation.image_prompt: Victorian parlour, dark bottle green damask wallpaper above a brown wood dado, black marble fireplace with a tall gilt overmantel mirror and crowded mantelpiece, button-back crimson velvet sofa, balloon-back chairs, round table with a fringed cloth, Turkey carpet, brass gasolier with glass shades, lace and heavy velvet curtains, ferns, framed pictures close together, warm dim light, rich and cluttered, interior photograph
implementation.negative_prompt: White walls, minimal, empty floor, bright daylight, modern furniture, chrome.
implementation.camera: 28 mm lens at 140 cm, three-quarter view from the door toward the hearth.
implementation.scene_3d: Room 500 x 450 cm, ceiling 330 cm. Daylight through lace at transmission 0.3; one 2200 K gasolier at 230 cm and three 1900 K table lamps.
furniture_list: chesterfield 200 x 90 x 75 cm, seat 44 cm

emotion.target_response: Enclosure: the viewer feels sheltered and a little overwhelmed, inside a warm, dim, crowded room.

avoid_when: The room is small and dark already.
The brief asks for calm, air or rooms that are easy to clean.

modifiers.how: Remove most objects, replace the damask with one handmade pattern, show the oak structure; keep the hearth.
Lighten the walls to a soft colour, keep the chintz and the collections, add skirted tables and humour.

sources.title: Charles Eastlake, Hints on Household Taste (London, 1868)
